newsitem.title: USA: Removing endrometriosis tissue improves fertility.
newsitem.headline: Removing endrometriosis tissue improves fertility.

text.p: Burning away some of the unnecessary tissue from the reproductive organs seems to make it easier for women with endometriosis to become pregnant, according to a study published in Thursday's New England Journal of Medicine.
Endometriosis, a condition where pieces of the lining of the uterus are found in other parts of the pelvis, affects about 2 to 3 percent of women who are in their childbearing years.
Among women who are infertile, 10 to 15 percent have endometriosis and about 30 to 40 percent of those are unable to have children.
In a test of 341 volunteers in 25 Canadian hospitals, a team led by Dr. Sylvie Marcoux of the University of Quebec Hospital Centre used a lighted tube to look for signs of the condition.
For half the women, the unwanted tissue was destroyed with electrocautery or a laser beam. In the remaining group the tissue was left alone.
The Marcoux group found that 31 percent of the women who had the tissue removed became pregnant within 36 weeks, compared to 17.7 percent of the women in the control group.

But in an editorial, Drs. Joseph C. Gambone and Alan H. DeCherney of the UCLA School of Medicine in Los Angeles cautioned that the results were not definitive because the women knew which treatment they had received.

That knowledge, they warned, "could have influenced their outlook and behaviour affecting fertility." Women who knew that their tissue had been removed might have been more enthusiastic about having sex which might have, in turn, increased their chances of conceiving.
Nonetheless, they said, the Marcoux experiment "is an important study of a controversial subject."
All of the volunteers had only mild or minimal amounts of endometriosis. Women with more severe cases were not studied.
The Marcoux team also concluded that removing the tissue in a woman with the condition does not affect her chances of having a miscarriage once she becomes pregnant.
